item.title: First attempt at an SCP: the girl with stag horns
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator pitch:
• An SCP that has minimal anomalous properties (enhanced senses, physiological abnormalities, Etc.) most of the time but it has an active time.
• During the active time it is extremely hostile and warps reality around it within a 20 Km radius.
Central Narrative: The SCP is found in a forest/cave system after several missing persons reports are filed for the area. The foundation acquires it at the end of it’s active time and it is compliant to the agents that were sent after it and it is placed in relatively low security. Exactly 11 months after the SCP is first acquired it enters its active state and breaches security.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reality warping effect causes the landscape to be a twisted, darkened version of the area that the SCP was found in. During its active period the SCP has a small radius that causes slowed cognitive ability
Additional Notes: Please tell me if any of these ideas boring, convoluted or stupid.

item.title: Inaccurate Extradimensional War Reenactment
item.description: Extradimensional beings who like to reenact human wars, but have a few of the details wrong.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A phenomenon that manifests near the locations and annual anniversaries of famous battles. Terrain and weather in the affected area reconfigure to match the original battle, and invisible and intangible entities manifest to reenact it, along with the appropriate military hardware, which is visible but still intangible. The Foundation initially thinks that these entities are ghosts, but they eventually notice that they’re sentient and aware of their surroundings, then attempts to make contact. The Foundation briefly speaks with the entities, enough to realize some humorous misconceptions the entities have about how human war works in three-dimensional space. Eventually, the entities manifest to reenact a battle that never happened. When the Foundation points this out, the entities realize they’re in the wrong universe and demanifest, never to return.

Central Narrative: The Foundation first discovers this phenomenon when it manifests near a populated area. There’s a log of notable manifestations (current list includes the Battles of Bull Run/Manassas, Hastings, Rorke’s Drift, and Megiddo, plus a prehistoric conflict between Homo sapiens and Neanderthals and a battle between the Mongols and Daevites). The log notes illustrate the Foundation’s dawning awareness of the entities’ sentience and attempts to interact, concluding with a final log of a manifestation somewhere in the Southern US that doesn’t correspond with any known battle. There are two addenda after that: one chronicling a humorous interaction between a Foundation personnel and one of the entities and one chronicling the final encounter with the anomaly, during which they realize they’re in the wrong place (“We’re in the wrong universe, you stupid idiot!”).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bait-and-switch of anomalies that seem to be ghosts but are actually slightly confused extradimensional war-reenacters is an amusing twist. I also intend to imply or even crosslink that the nonexistent battle is the one described by SCP-592. I plan to eventually write a Tale about the universe full of faceless people described by that book and encountered in SCP-970.

Additional Notes: I’m not sure if I should have the anomalies manifest at the actual locations of the battles or on some shapeshifting island or something out in the middle of nowhere. Having them at the actual locations requires all sorts of memetic/amnestic foolery on the part of the Foundation and/or the entities to preserve normalcy, which I worry would bloat the Description and stretch suspension of disbelief.

item.title: The Tainted Saint Collection (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Parasitic donor organs that, following surgical implantation, rot and digest their hosts.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Euclid-class collection of parasitic donor organs that are capable of osmotic extracellular digestion. Individual "fragments" of SCP-XXXX possess passive, non-lethal cognitohazardous properties.

Central Narrative: The Tainted Saint Collection is the first entry in a wider narrative I have planned. It's centered around the research of Dr. Lee Elliot, an ex-field agent with an interest in SCPs that can manipulate organic matter. I intend for this narrative to begin (temporally) with a different SCP, an incident report, and a Tale. However, this SCP seemed like a better place to start in practice since it's easier to pitch.

The report starts out normal, with little off-kilter details sprinkled in to breed unease. Note, I described SCP-XXXX as a collection of donor organs in the intro here, but in the article itself that information will not be revealed until the description section. By the time the reader reaches that point, I want them to be hyperaware of the danger associated with even brief contact so the reveal that they were implanted into people hits as hard as possible.

Beyond that, the bulk of the article's narrative will follow the background of each fragment individually, outlining their quirks. SCP-XXXX-B, for example, kills its hosts within a few days, whereas SCP-XXXX-A remained inside the same host for six months. At the end, I plan on including a brief interview between SCP-XXXX-A's ex-host and Dr. Elliot. Lastly, I'll include a short lab report detailing a non-lethal vivisection of SCP-XXXX-A that ended up costing Dr. Elliot his left eye. Spoiler alert: fragments of SCP-XXXX are immobile by choice, not biology.

Hook/Attention Grabber: They're carnivorous donor organs with cognitohazardous properties. I know I'd read an article about that.

Additional Notes: I have way too much experience writing formal academic prose, so my main concern is getting the lore/terminology right. I'm also wondering if anyone knows some good SCPs that introduce recurring researcher characters without making that introduction too intrusive. I don't want the article to end up feeling like it's about Dr. Elliot.

item.title: Medicine Man - first scp idea
item.description: My first scp idea (seeking greenlight). About a sculpture that invades one's consciousness when activated. This new consciousness has a vast knowledge of chemistry and biology.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • The Medicine Man is a sculpture that activates when an individual lowers their guard or gets distracted within the statue's area of effect. The victim is unaware of this, but will see the manifestation of the sculpture's consciousness (as in "its soul"), which calls itself The Medicine Man. Once confronted with the medicine man, said individual will never be able to fully focus/concentrate again (unknowingly), which makes the individual more vulnerable to the sculpture's effect. When exposed to the statue for too long, one could enter a comatose state or develop Alzheimer's.
  • When trying to prevent an individual from totally succumbing to the medicine man by attempting to improve their ability to focus with external forces (caffeine, adrenaline injection, etc.), Medicine Man will switch said individual's consciousness with itself, trapping the individual consciousness in the statue. Medicine Man can then host a body until it finds another statue to reside in.

Central Narrative:
Medicine Man traveled from sculpture to sculpture, while leaving behind a trail of corrupted minds. This is how the foundation found him.
Inside the foundation, Medicine Man is appreciated for its vast amount of knowledge about chemistry and biology and is sometimes given a host to be interviewed by researchers.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Opposite of cognitohazard that corrupts the mind without the victim knowing, which I personally find quite creepy

Additional Notes:
I had already started a draft in the sandbox because I didn't know i needed a greenlight.

item.title: Anomalous Trauma [Seeking Greenlights]
item.description: A teenager who is unable to move on from a traumatic event, both mentally and physically.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Potentially horror

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: A teenager who is unable to move on from a traumatic event, both mentally and physically.

Central Narrative: The SCP is a person who is unable to age, heal from wounds, or die, due to an incident where they were attacked. They believe themself to be dead. Although initially hostile to the Foundation, they bond with a specific researcher who ends up breaking them out.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The specifics of the attack are initially unclear and the reader has to piece it together from various hints.

Additional Notes: I'm a bit hesitant about the "escape" thing. I feel like, in a narrative/emotional sense, it's the only conclusion that works, but from a logical standpoint, I'm not sure how viable it is. In general, I'm not sure how easy this will be to pull off. Any responses about that would be great.

item.title: Time: Limited
item.description: "Your protection is no longer possible, we are sorry."
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: A series of interstellar radio signals make their way to earth, warning of an impending threat. After the first message, the foundation ensures no other stations can receive the signals.

Central Narrative: After determining the radio signal's origin to be extraterrestrial, the foundation sets about discovering what sent it, why it was sent, where it was sent from, what the threat is, why "protection" is no longer possible, and why it was needed. The answers to these questions are vague, with the threat remaining unknown and the senders of the radio signal also remaining unknown.

However, it is discovered that the signal originated from the Canis Major Dwarf Galaxy, and it is assumed this possible threat the senders were protecting us from likely originated from the same galaxy. This assumption is later confirmed when foundation astronomers discover an abnormal mass exiting the galaxy, with a trajectory towards earth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The containment procedures for when the mass arrives at earth, which suggest that, if the mass cannot be neutralized and is a threat to all civilisation, then a full planetary evacuation is to commence. My hope is that this will coax the reader into reading deeper.

Additional Notes: Currently N/A.

item.title: An Old Theater (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: "It burned down during a play. I saw it collapse, I heard the screams. Believe me when I say whatever brought it back is not Safe, maybe not even Euclid"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Commonplace SCP article layout, with Interviews, Exploration Logs, and addendums.

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation contains an old theater once an entire town's population seems to disappear into it on re-opening night. Inside, the Foundation finds spatial anomalies; flesh-eating and mind-controlling fungi; and a creature hewn together from corpses that desperately wants to exit the building to "follow it's directive".

Central Narrative: The article's Special Containment Procedures seemed to be overly detailed and specialized for an Euclid, until the head researcher revealed to have lived in that town and that they knew just what happened the first time the theatre opened (interviews). The fungi within is observed to interfere with electronic equipment within the building, and it seems mainly to grow from the creature’s blood and secretions. When d-class are sent to investigate with less specialized transmission equipment, they discover a seemingly endless series of waiting rooms, storage areas, backstages, and stages filled with decaying props. The props and hints towards the play performed vary wildly from room to room, and the one room the d-class seem to find but not explore is a basement, from where the creature emerges and kills most of the d-class in the exploration party; those who survived ended up proving the contagious capabilities of the fungus inside and were terminated.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature within stitches all those who it manages to catch onto itself, through a redacted procedure observed through drone observation (exploration logs). And it is stated that there was one time the creature actually managed to breach containment, and in the time it took Foundation personnel to find out where the creature had gone, it managed to decimate the entire population of a city, level several buildings, and almost open a portal into an unknown dimension possibly filled with creatures alike it. The creature’s sudden increase in capabilities when outside containment proved that the building’s anomalous properties seem to aid in the containment of the creature.

Additional Notes: The Article’s series of addendums let it be known that the creature, the last times it’s been seen by personnel within the building, has been covered in water or has left humid footprints. After analyzing the remains of this water, it is found to be that of the abandoned town’s sewer system. The petition to include the sewer system into the containment procedure, or to force its collapse through demolition charges was left pending.

item.title: How Long Can We Wait? - Cognitohazard SCP
item.description: There are 3 parts to the skip, a cognitohazard, an anomalous creature, and a dangerous site.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

Essentially, there are 3 parts to this SCP:
- The first is a cognitohazardous message. Once you read it, it will stay in your mind, slowly growing in you consciousness, eventually replacing all other thoughts, shutting down your motor functions, and killing you, as you will forget how to breathe. This cognitohazard can also be spread, and creates a strong desire in the infected to visit the second part of this skip.
- The second is an anomalous creature. It is located in a pit, and anyone who approaches or enters the pit will be filled with an extremely strong hatred towards the creature, and a powerful desire to end its life. The foundation believes, however, that if this creature were to die, it would result in an end-of-the-world scenario.
- The final part is a site, believed by the foundation to be the origin of the apocalypse should the creature ever be killed. the site is marked by a ring of 5 statues, 1 resembling the creature in the pit, and the other resembling redacted creatures that the foundation has already encountered. Additionally, every month, a creature spawns at this location, which must immediately be terminated by foundation personnel.

+ Rest of the post
- hide

[Central Narrative:
There isn't exactly a narrative per se, but the reader will slowly uncover more information about the SCP, and how the different parts of it relate together. Essentially, the message will draw the victim to the creature in the pit, and once they get there they will be compelled to kill the creature, beginning the apokalypse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I feel like the cognitohazard is a fairly unique premise, and the chain of events that could so easily lead to the apokalypse.

Additional Notes:
Considering going more in-depth through addendums as to who the other 4 statues are. They would be deceased creatures that the foundation has already encountered, implying that all five must be killed in order to free some cosmic being, and the creature in the pit is the last remaining "lock" if you will.]

item.title: A parallel world
item.description: There's a parallel world that exists around us but the only way to experience and investigate it is through its interaction with two ancient artifacts.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: There's a parallel world that exists around us but the only way to experience and investigate it is through its interaction with two ancient artifacts.

Central Narrative: Two disk-like artifacts are discovered which seem to be welded together with some gear-like items (hinting at ancient machinery). The gear-like parts of the artifacts do not exist in our world, they seem to exist in a parallel world nut since they are welded with the disk-like parts they move together as one. Through experimentation and various incidents involving the two artifacts, few things about the parallel world are discovered: it's filled with a low density fluid, there is occasional turbulence, a variety of unexplained sounds, temperature variations and most likely some kind of entity (or entities).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The parallel world and our limited understanding of it, since everything we discover about it has to be learned by indirectly interacting with it through the two artifacts.

Additional Notes: I've already written a 1600 words draft. I also intend to attach a drawing, a photo and a few sound recordings.

item.title: SCP that preys on sex predators (Trigger Warning: Description of an Abuser and his crimes)
item.description: A creature with a boundless hatred of sexual predators uses a combination of mental manipulation and shapeshifting to lure and brutally murder predators. The predator of predators
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Idea Pitch
Idea Pitch


Elevator Pitch: The basic idea for this SCP is a creature who commits acts of horrific violence against people who are considered to be one of the most repulsive kind of people alive (sexual predators). Despite the cruel and sometimes downright evil nature of the creature the audience can't help but root for it sometimes as the details of it's murders are revealed through reports and interviews.

Central Narrative: The LAPD are investigating a string of murders, the victims are all men and women either accused or found guilty of sexual abuse. The only other thing connecting the victims is that they were all last spotted with a different person who the police can find no records proving they exist. As there are so far 15 victims and 15 people with no proof of existence it has the police both confused and at a loss for what to do.

A Foundation mole inside the LAPD brings the case to the attention of the Foundation who find the circumstances suspicious and decide to investigate themselves. Eventually after tracking potential victims in the area they catch the creature in the act, taking the form of an attractive secretary it has lured the Reigional Manager of a local tobacco company (who has been using his power to sexually harrass, grope and pressure young female employees and interns into sex) into bed. Only to use non human apendages to slit the man's throat and begin mutilating his corpse.

The Foundation capture and contain the creature, bringing it back for further study. Where it's psychology, biology, nature, abilites of mental manipulation and shapeshifting are researched by the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A vicious and psychotic creature that rather than doing the standard killing of innocent people to satisfy a bloodlust, is targetting and punishing those that arguably deserve what they are getting.

Additional Notes: The subject of sexual assualt and abuse is a very sensetive issue, this SCP idea is not intended to make light of these issues. Rather show them for what they are; evil and dispicable. As well helping readers to vent thir frustrations about these issues by seeing predators get served unmerciful justice. It's not my intention to make survivors relive their trauma so if this idea makes it to draft a trigger warning will be provided.

item.title: The Grand Conspiracy (No Longer Active)
item.description: OK, thanks for the ideas, I've almost made up my mind for this to be a tale, I'll repost this again when I come up with a plot and details for greenlights.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No, I want to see if people think it will work as an SCP and then develop it a bit more first

Page Type: SCP article? Maybe Tale?

Genre: Comedy, History??

Elevator Pitch: A viral Youtube video connecting a lot of the popular theories, things ranging from the Paul is dead theory, The Denver Airport, to the Black Knight Satellite, except this time the Foundation is thrown in and said to be the reason this all happened. The video has no anomalous properties, but it poses a threat to the secrecy of the Foundation.

Central Narrative: The idea isn’t fully fleshed out yet, but what I am aiming for is it to tell a story about the Foundation that connects about four to five popular conspiracy theories, with neutralized SCP reports, breach reports, operation reports, and all of those mixed in. The theory will likely be super far-fetched, and the reports featured in the video are speculated to be fakes, which leads to the comedy at the end - When in the form of an addendum, one of the personnel hints at some, if not all of the theory being true.

Hook/Attention Grabber: I think mainly the hook would be how the Foundation is connected to all of the theories, it’s going to be difficult but I want to write a lot of real-life events into it and explain it as an effect due to the Foundation.

Additional Notes: The reason why this isn’t something like an incident report is that the video was never taken down, due to the fact that it went viral within twenty-four hours and the Foundation doesn’t have a way to track and supply amnestics to all the people who watched it. They conducted an operation that tries to influence the video to be viewed as a joke instead. Also, this may confuse some of you, so I’ll make it a bit clearer, but all the theories will be a chain of events, not a collection of events handled by the Foundation separately.

item.title: Twisting Termite Tunnels
item.description: Seems like the little buggers can get into anything...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not yet, I suppose…?

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi, Nature Documentary, Comedy(?)

Elevator Pitch: Termites with a nest-building behavior that can bypass conventional spatial limitations, including covering immense distances and moving in and out of perfectly sealed spaces. Pretty much the same goals, needs, and individual intelligence of ordinary termites in all other respects.

Central Narrative: The first clue is the identification of Australian compass termites somewhere that they definitely should not be. Further investigation leads to exploration of their tunnels and the discovery that distant places are connected through seemingly-random twists and turns, which the insects have no trouble navigating but are confusing to a human sense of direction. There's a conspicuous lack of pocket dimensions, thaumaturgical Ways, or significant gravitational anomalies involved, at least as far as the Foundation can initially detect.

The Foundation would be up against mundane technological limitations on what sort of equipment can fit down an individual termite tunnel, as any substantial damage to the structures promptly collapses their anomalous effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: We have an otherwise mostly mundane (if highly industrious) social insect species that cannot be reliably confined to a single habitat, although it's not an immediate Veil risk unless people start trying to identify individual termite species. What's more, they've created a functional hyperspace network out of nothing but soil and their own feces - and wouldn't the Foundation just love to learn how that works?

Additional Notes: Researching mundane eusocial insects is still relatively cutting-edge science, since they tend to live underground and it's hard to study large-scale emergent behaviors outside their natural habitat. I intend to research more into the kinds of technology used for these purposes, and play with how the Foundation might take them further. I could see this having a lot of experiment logs - perhaps taking reader suggestions, if the article were to take off.

item.title: Reluctant Wendigo
item.description: A young man that can turn into a wendigo made of volcanic glass, whether he wants to or not.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Folklore/Drama/a slight bit of humor.

Page Layout: Standard Description and Containment Procedures, interview, incident report, and requests. The SCP and its procedures are currently under review by the foundation ethics committee.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a young man that experiences anomalous growths over any injury he receives. If the injury is enough to incapacitate or "kill" the subject it will instead become enveloped in this obsidian-like substance[in the visage of a wendigo from Algonquin folklore] and attempt to consume the flesh of any organism it can. It must be noted that this material is impenetrable to known conventional means.

+ Central Narrative, Hook and Additional Notes
- collapse

Central Narrative: XXXX was discovered wandering along the highway after it was hit and incapacitated in a car crash on the I-15. Police reports indicate it terminated both the driver and all but one family member in the car before fleeing. Early interviews in containment suggest the entity gained its anomalous properties after being forced into a sanitarium for divergent behavior. This asylum practiced unsanctioned, immoral "treatments" on XXXX that would leave it with its anomalous properties. Basically, imagine "The Factory" but instead of churning out anomalous objects its anomalous humanoid entities.

While in containment the head researcher assigned for XXXX, Dr. Pharrow, interviews it for several psychological evaluations and learns of the existence of "Lindvell's Sanitorium for Ordinary Youth!" where each patient is somehow given anomalous properties to 'protect' or make 'useful' for potential adoptive parties. A later incident report indicates that an associate of Lindvell's Sanitorium facilitated a containment breach to retrieve XXXX for a "prospective and interested party." It is also within this report where it is discovered that XXXX can be knocked from its incapacitated state by sustained impacts from high velocity, high density projectiles.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A young man is forced to become an anomaly he has no control over. His body's defense mechanisms are hijacked, he cant die, only sent into a feral ravenous, starving state that spurs him to kill, to satiate.

Additional Notes: I…plan to pursue this sanitarium idea further in SCP Tales. I've most likely explained this poorly, and I apologize if so. Please do not hesitate to reply with questions or queries for clarification. Also if there is a similar SCP somewhere, please tell me, there are thousands of entries and I am incapable of trawling through every one.

item.title: Mr. Ink
item.description: Think: one of the enemies from BATIM, but more fleshed out and very much a sadistic prick.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): -

Page Layout (Optional): -

Elevator Pitch: Mx. Ink (or Mr. Ink, any is fine) is a humanoid entity created as part of the Little Misters line. Their appearance varies, but is often reminiscent of a mime (minus the makeup, just the white face.) They're made up of a dense, tar-like substance and posses no real organs or anything similar to human anatomy. This would be the ink they're named after.

Due to their sadistic, cunning nature, Mr. Ink are contained in an air-tight metal barrel, thus preventing them from just going out and torturing any unsuspecting researcher. Since the liquid is so dense, Mr. Ink can make it seem like there's more of it than there actually is by making it less dense at will. They can't control the liquid unless it's all in one glob, if that makes any sense.

Apart from being able to control their body as a liquid, Mr. Ink can insert themselves into any text they come in contact with, though the text has to be written in black ink. (This part can be removed, since I know of other SCPs that do the text-changing trick)

Central Narrative: A little mister that will make all your stories more interesting! Careful, though, they're a bit snappy.

Mr. Ink was contained after a string of mysterious and twisted murders in a quiet neighborhood somewhere in London. They continually attempt to breach containment, and frequently resort to torturing researchers and interviewers they have access to.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As the SCP can manipulate texts to include them, it's up for debate if they're actually part of the Little Misters line, or just stole a Little Misters tag and added themselves to it for some reason.

Additional Notes: -

I have more ideas for this, so please feel free to ask questions if you want! This is my second SCP idea, so I'm still pretty inexperienced. I don't 100% get the new format either, so there's probably some info I've left out.

The two clouds that obviously allow you to teleport to eachother are antipodal to eachother, and can only be entered through the top (it maintains velocity). They are static in the sky. Under each of the clouds are families that are linked (somewhat)

The families contain a father, mother, two children of indeterminent gender, and a dog, all of which look very similar. They are likely in contact with eachother, and despite the appearance similarities, are very different people. This is another aspect that I plan to flesh out a lot more (interview logs, experiments, addendums galore)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is based around a cloud, which is something that not many scps do. It also could be used to explain possible events in history, or something along those lines. The idea of a wormhole has been done a lot before, but i imagine that this object also has some amount of gravitational effect, leading to a possible earlier discovery than that of plane travel.

item.title: The Indigo Branch (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A dark web page that lists the names of many different people, ranked from 1 to 100. Each name is accompanied by a price, and the names change almost daily. Anyone who views the site will always end up on the list and disappear sometime in the future.

Central Narrative: A recent suicide in urban California has a man dead at his computer, a note at his side, and a bullet through his head. The paper talks of the Indigo Branch, and how to get to it on the dark web. It also talks about how the man had received a steady amount of cryptocurrency over the past few months, and with his life in a bad situation, began using the money in an effort to turn everything around. The sender quickly begins talking to him, and says they will continue giving him money as long as he uses his coding knowledge to help locate information on the people whose names appear on the site. He soon stops helping the anonymous sender, and finds his name in the seventh spot on the list within a few days. He decided to kill himself rather than face the online criminals for his mistake.

+ show block
– hide block

An interested Foundation personnel looks deeper into this case, and starts using the site to track down the people he sees high up on the list. He finds that they all disappear at seemingly random times, some only hours after being on the list, and others who never disappeared before the personnel went missing himself. Because of the bizarre way these people go missing - seeming to vanish out of thin air most times - the Indigo Branch was categorized as an anomaly, and is only viewable by those with higher clearance.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Instead of another entity that just rips your face off for looking at it, or a spooky room that turns you into a chair, the Indigo Branch is just a single web page with names and numbers, who change at random intervals and correspond to real people. Less than being horrifying, this SCP is mysterious, allowing the reader to interpret everything in their own way.

Additional Notes: My biggest concern here is if I mistakenly wrote something that has already been written and solidified as an SCP. There are so many out there, and I have only read a few here and there, that is is a distinct possibility it may already exist. If this is the case, please let me know! (Other feedback on the idea itself is always welcome, of course)

item.title: My joke scp idea. SCP-5127-J
item.description: I pasted the description of my scp. The name of this scpp is " Thats what she said")
item.content:encoded: SCP-5127-J is a translucent ghost version of Michael Gary Scott, the branch manager of Dunder Mifflin Scranton SCP-5127-J first appeared when Steve Carell finished The Office in 2011. Before the foundation knew anything about SCP-5127-J, It was roaming Steve Carell's mansion. After Steve Carrel said anything, SCP-5127-J responded with "That's what she said" which made anything Steve said seem wrong. It happened so frequently, Steve Carrel began to lose money from low self esteem and stress. The foundation kept his losses under wraps as they would eventually ruin his career. He wrote letters to the producers and begged them to let him back on to the show. Eventually in the last episode, They let him back in. For a while during the recording, SCP-5127-J was silent. But when they aired the episode, SCP-5127-J came back. The first instance after the show was when Steve was cleaning up after the family meal and he said," I'm going to put this back." and SCP-5127-J responded," That's what she said." Recently the foundation has recorded 600,000 USD that Steve Carrel has lost to SCP-5127-J.
